question: Which of the following museum is situated in Kerala? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Napier Museum
Salar Jung Museum
Albert Hall Museum
Dakshinachitra Museum
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Napier Museum

Explanation:
Napier Museum is a renowned museum located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India. Established in 1855, it is named after Francis Napier, the Governor of Madras Presidency. The museum houses a rich collection of artifacts, sculptures, paintings, and historical objects showcasing the cultural heritage of South India. It is also famous for its unique architectural style blending Kerala, Chinese, and Mughal influences. Other options: Salar Jung Museum is in Hyderabad (Telangana), Albert Hall Museum is in Jaipur (Rajasthan), and Dakshinachitra Museum is in Chennai (Tamil Nadu). Thus, Napier Museum is the correct answer as it is the only museum located in Kerala.

question: Which country's President suggested the name "United Nations"? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Russia
United States of America
France
Germany
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is United States of America

Explanation:
The name "United Nations" was suggested by US President Franklin D. Roosevelt. It was first used in the Declaration by United Nations on 1 January 1942, when 26 nations pledged to fight together against the Axis powers. Later, in 1945, the San Francisco Conference adopted the UN Charter. Roosevelt chose this name to symbolize the unity and cooperation of nations in the fight for peace and freedom.

question: Which temple is known as 'black pagoda'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Konark Sun Temple
Suryanar Temple
Martand Sun Temple
Shani Shingnapur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Konark Sun Temple

Explanation:
The Konark Sun Temple is famously known as the 'Black Pagoda'. Located in Odisha, India, it was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I. This temple is dedicated to the Sun God and is renowned for its unique architecture resembling a massive chariot with 12 wheels and seven horses. It has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The name 'Black Pagoda' originates from its dark stone construction, giving it a blackish appearance. The temple is a masterpiece of Kalinga architecture and attracts numerous tourists and devotees worldwide.

question: Who was the secretary of UNO between the year 1997-2006? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Ban ki-Moon
Trigvi Li
U-Thant
Kofi Annan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kofi Annan

Explanation:
From 1997 to 2006, the seventh Secretary-General of the United Nations was Kofi Annan. He was a citizen of Ghana and the first African to serve as Secretary-General, completing two terms (1997-2006). During his tenure, the UN focused on peacekeeping, human rights, and the Millennium Development Goals. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001. Before him, Boutros Boutros-Ghali served (1992-1996), and after him, Ban Ki-moon (2007-2016) took office.

question: The United Nations organisation was set up through the signing of the United Nations Charter by ______ states. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (14/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: 180
51
84
200
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 51

Explanation:
The United Nations Organisation (UNO) was established on 24 October 1945. Its Charter was signed by 50 countries in San Francisco on 26 June 1945, and Poland later signed, bringing the total to 51 founding member states. It was created after World War II to maintain international peace and security. Most of the 51 founding members were from Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Currently, the UN has 193 member states.

question: Who was the second person to land on the moon? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (14/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Buzz Aldrin
Charles Conrad
Alan Shepard
Alan L Bean
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Buzz Aldrin

Explanation:
The first person to land on the moon was Neil Armstrong, who stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission. The second person was Buzz Aldrin, who landed on the moon in the same mission. Aldrin and Armstrong spent about 2.5 hours on the lunar surface, while Michael Collins orbited the moon in the command module. Buzz Aldrin played a key role in planting the American flag and conducting scientific experiments on the moon. Charles Conrad was the third person on Apollo 12, Alan Shepard the fifth on Apollo 14, and Alan Bean the fourth on Apollo 12.

question: When were the caves of Bhimbetka discovered? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (14/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1957-58
1954-55
1955-56
1953-54
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1957-58

Explanation:
The caves of Bhimbetka are located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh. They were discovered in 1957-58 by Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar. This site provides significant evidence of prehistoric human life. The caves contain rock paintings from the Paleolithic to the Medieval period. Bhimbetka was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003. It is under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

question: The original name of Mahabharata is: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (15/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Jaya Samhita
Bhrigu Samhita
Shiva Samhita
Sushruta Samhita
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jaya Samhita

Explanation:
The original name of Mahabharata is Jaya Samhita. It was composed by Sage Vedavyasa. Initially, it was known as Jaya, meaning victory. Later, it was expanded and called Bharata and finally Mahabharata. The epic contains one lakh shlokas, making it the longest epic in the world. It is not just a story of war but also includes ethics, philosophy, and religion. The Bhagavad Gita, a key philosophical text, is a part of the Bhishma Parva of Mahabharata.

☛ How many shlokas are in Mahabharata? → One lakh
☛ In which parva is Bhagavad Gita located? → Bhishma Parva
☛ What does Jaya mean? → Victory
☛ What is the literal meaning of Jaya Samhita? → Samhita of Victory

शिव संहिता
सुश्रुत संहिता
solution_hi:

Explanation:
महाभारत का मूल नाम जय संहिता है। इस महाकाव्य की रचना वेदव्यास जी ने की थी। इसे पहले जय नाम से जाना जाता था, जिसका अर्थ विजय है। बाद में इसमें विस्तार किया गया और इसे भारत तथा अंत में महाभारत कहा जाने लगा। महाभारत में कुल एक लाख श्लोक हैं, जो इसे विश्व का सबसे बड़ा महाकाव्य बनाते हैं। यह ग्रंथ न केवल युद्ध की कथा है, बल्कि इसमें नीति, दर्शन और धर्म का विवरण मिलता है। भीष्म पर्व में स्थित भगवद गीता इसी ग्रंथ का एक महत्वपूर्ण भाग है।
